model_annotation: The image displays two stacked bar charts side by side, both illustrating the development of public sector expenditures as a percentage of GDP (% des BIP¹) from 1991 to 2023, with a vertical dashed line marking the year 2000 and an arrow labeled "Bahnreform²" (Railway Reform) indicating a structural change around that time. The left chart shows the breakdown of expenditures by level of government: blue bars represent the federal government (Bund), purple bars the Länder (federal states), and green bars the municipalities (Gemeinden). The total height of each stacked bar corresponds to the overall public expenditure as a percentage of GDP, which fluctuates over time, peaking around 1991 at approximately 3.2% and again around 2019 at about 3.0%, with a dip to around 2.4% in 2000. The right chart displays the net change in public expenditures (i.e., the difference between expenditures and revenues or the fiscal balance) for each level of government, with the same color coding, and a black line indicating the total for all public authorities (Gebietskörperschaften insgesamt). In this chart, the values are mostly close to zero, with some negative values (deficits) and positive values (surpluses) over time, and the total line (black) shows a general decline from around 0.8% in 1991 to near zero by 2023, with a notable dip below zero around 2005–2006. Both charts share the same horizontal axis (years) and vertical axis (percentage of GDP, ranging from -0.5 to 3.5), and the bars are arranged chronologically from left to right.
